findings.title: Reject ties between the highest-priority crypto providers
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return priority 200. When more than one is present, this sort preserves their ServiceLoader encounter order and silently selects the first. In particular, if the default implementation is encountered before the FIPS implementation, cryptographic operations use the non-FIPS implementation despite the FIPS provider being present. The previous implementation rejected this ambiguous configuration. Retain a fail-fast check for tied highest-priority providers while allowing the lower-priority authz provider to coexist.

findings.title: The abstract order method breaks existing provider implementations
findings.body: Adding order() as an abstract interface method breaks already-compiled CryptoProvider implementations. When an existing implementation is loaded alongside the newly registered authz provider, the sorting comparator invokes order() on both and throws AbstractMethodError for the existing implementation, preventing crypto initialization. Provide a backward-compatible default priority that preserves existing full providers' precedence over the lightweight authz provider.

findings.title: Exercise the matching curves for ES384 and ES512
findings.body: The EC key generator is never initialized with the curve for the algorithm under test, so on OpenJDK all three tests use the default P-256 key. Consequently, testES512 never exercises a real P-521 signature, whose DER sequence normally exceeds 127 bytes and requires the new encoder and decoder's long-form length handling. Initialize keys with secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 respectively, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA so the tests establish signature correctness rather than only converter self-consistency.
